deviations_assessed.c_s4_commit_tree: UPHELD. Re-merging an already-merged branch is a no-op, so the brief's 'merge twice' construction cannot produce a second merge commit. The brief explicitly allowed a documented alternative construction.

blocking_finding.summary: INV-3 fail-open: the discriminator trusts two mutable DECLARED fields, so a never-integrated parallel-lane WP can be stamped MERGED with a forged merged_commit simply by writing branch == base_branch.
blocking_finding.mechanism: wp_tip and base_tip are both resolved from BRANCH NAMES. When the status claims the sequential layout both resolve to the same commit, so the :371 `is-ancestor X X` precondition is trivially true. git.commit -- the field that records the WP's real work tip -- is only checked for non-emptiness and never participates in any topology check.
blocking_finding.reproduced: Orchestrator built a repo with an unmerged feature/x, forged a status claiming branch=base_branch=main while git.commit stayed the unmerged feature tip, and ran the real wrapper: FINALIZE_OK, state=MERGED, merged_commit set to the main tip -- a commit unrelated to the WP's work, which remained unintegrated.
